subject: Texas AI Docket, Carousel No. 14, September 3rd, 2026, Who gets an invitation
body:
Who gets an invitation

Carousel No. 14, September 3rd, 2026

Did NOT meet the bar: 6.762 against 6.8. Read before posting.

This run did not merge, so the images below come from the run branch claude/daily-2026-09-03 rather than from main. They stop resolving if that branch is deleted.

What degraded

  • The Supabase connector is not available in this session, so the scanner's daily cap query could not run for the second consecutive day. Recorded, not worked around.
  • Phase 12's pixel critics were not spawned. The panel of three did that work across five rounds instead, and every defect they found is in the run record.
  • The West Campus Data Center is named in the caption and on no frame. Slide 3 has no room for a fourth line without its dek striking a drawn rule, which qa.py caught when it was tried.
  • Nine focal rectangles in the storyboard are still BOUNDING BOXES rather than the objects they name, so slide 6's two slots measure 5.7 percent as a box and about 1.3 as drawn. Both round 5 judges named the same fix and it is out of reach from here.
  • A review bot on PR 252 filed seven findings after the panel closed and six were real. One was a P1. tx-2026-0038 was stamped verified while two of its claims sat on a page no client here can read a quote from, and both are now removed rather than re-stamped. All six are fixed. Correcting the ERCOT flag on the nationwide CFTC notice widened a published field's type, so schema_contract is a third blocker and it needs one command from a maintainer, python3 scripts/site/schema_contract.py --update

Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

Post this

Upload the PDF to LinkedIn as a document, title it Who gets an invitation, paste the post copy under it, then paste the first comment within a minute of posting.

carousel.pdf   contact sheet   the site

1. The post copy

Who gets an invitation?

The Texas A&M University System's VISION supercomputer ranked No. 66 in the world at 34.82 petaflops measured. It sits in the West Campus Data Center at Texas A&M University.

VISION's own documentation states the present condition. Access is invitation-only and approved via TAMUS governance. The current status is controlled beta.

Two System pages describe who VISION is for. Both use the future tense. One reads "VISION will be available to researchers of all disciplines across the entire Texas A&M System".

Onboarding is expected to begin with the institutions that finished integration, and the front page is seeking beta testers. The documentation states the access rule and states no number. How many researchers can use it today?

#TexasAMSystem #VISIONsupercomputer #TOP500

What this deck does not say, because the sources do not.

TOP500 publishes no university category. Neither its list page nor its system detail page calls
VISION the fastest university supercomputer in the United States. That framing belongs to the
System and to Tarleton State, and VISION's own site says only that it is one of the
highest-performing AI supercomputers at any North American university.

No page fetched names a county or a city for the West Campus Data Center, so this record names
none.

No dated Board of Regents action was found. The newsroom states the approval and gives no
meeting date and no agenda item.

The compound counts are printed as their own sources wrote them and are never joined. Nothing
in the record connects them, and about a week is not a duration this record can turn into a rate.

The full entry, with every claim and every source, is on the record at texasaidocket.com

The machine changed itself

  • CAPTION_CRAFT.md now separates a closing move's SUBSTANCE from its FORM and gives four of five an interrogative rendering
    Every caption from August 25th to September 2nd closed the same way, seven runs. August 25th is the day caption_check began enforcing brand.yaml's ends_with, and 'ask the one question' is the only one of the five closes interrogative on its face. A gate forced the repetition and the doctrine kept listing four moves nobody could spend
  • ledger_check now checks whether the caption room OBEYED the three exclusion lists, not only that they were derived correctly
    Replayed against the shipped ledger, eight entries used a move their own window covered and the gate was green on every one. It binds from today forward, because captions.json is append only and a permanently red gate is one somebody switches off
  • caption_check and claims_check now say something the reader did not already know, and claims_check imports the record's own source vocabulary rather than copying it
    The ends_with message named a rule and not the collision behind it. claims_check held a second copy of docket_build.SOURCE_TYPES that had silently diverged on two words

Each reverts on its own commit.

This is a draft. Nothing was sent. The deck did NOT merge, so nothing here is on main and there is nothing to post. The links resolve against the run branch for as long as it exists.
